message:
Migrate to Microsoft Foundry account + project (resolves #3084) (#3158)

* Migrate to Azure AI Foundry account + project

Deploy the Azure AI account as an Azure AI Foundry account (kind: 'AIServices'
with allowProjectManagement) and create a Foundry project inside it, replacing
the classic kind: 'OpenAI' account. Models are still deployed on the account, so
the backend endpoint (*.openai.azure.com) and all AZURE_OPENAI_* env vars are
unchanged.

- Add infra/core/ai/ai-foundry-project.bicep: project resource + project-scoped
  RBAC (Azure AI Project Manager for the deploying user, Azure AI User for the
  backend identity) + name/endpoint outputs.
- Bump the account AVM module to 0.15.0 for allowProjectManagement support.
- Gate Foundry behavior on self-created accounts only: bring-your-own accounts
  (AZURE_OPENAI_SERVICE set) keep their existing kind and get no project, so
  classic Azure OpenAI accounts keep working unchanged.
- Refactor private-endpoints.bicep to support multiple DNS zones per endpoint;
  the Foundry PE resolves services.ai.azure.com in addition to openai.azure.com
  and cognitiveservices.azure.com.
- Add FOUNDRY_PROJECT_NAME / FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT outputs and wire
  foundryProjectName through main.parameters.json and both CI pipelines.
- Document BYO behavior in docs/deploy_existing.md.

Resolves #3084

Co-authored-by: (a person) <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Ignore compiled Bicep output (infra/main.json)

`az bicep build` emits infra/main.json / infra/main.test.json next to the
templates; these are build artifacts and should never be committed.

Co-authored-by: (a person) <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fully skip Azure OpenAI provisioning for bring-your-own accounts

Previously the openAi AVM module still ran for bring-your-own (BYO)
existing accounts, upserting the account and pushing model deployments,
which made the conditional logic hard to follow. Now the module only
runs on a fresh Foundry deploy (deployFoundryAccount). For BYO we skip
the account, model deployments, Foundry project, and private endpoint
entirely, only keeping the RG-scoped role assignments the app's managed
identity needs.

- Gate openAi module and its private endpoint on deployFoundryAccount
- Simplify the module (always AIServices + allowProjectManagement) and
  the private-endpoint DNS zone list (always the three Foundry zones)
- Add openAiServiceNameResolved / openAiEndpointResolved helper vars so
  env vars + outputs work across fresh / BYO-existing / custom paths;
  BYO endpoint is string-built to match the backend's derivation
- Document that BYO users must pre-create model deployments and manage
  their own private networking

* Fix BYO gating: deploy Foundry account on openAiHost intent, not openAiServiceName

AZURE_OPENAI_SERVICE is also a bicep output azd persists after every deploy,
so gating deployFoundryAccount on empty(openAiServiceName) wrongly skipped the
account on redeploys. Gate on isAzureOpenAiHost && deployAzureOpenAi (matching
upstream); azure_custom remains the don't-touch BYO path. Reuse openAiServiceName
for the account name/subdomain idempotently. Fix docs note accordingly.

* fix(infra): keep Foundry template in classic ARM mode to avoid RG collision

Pin the openAi AVM account module to 0.14.0 (was 0.15.0) and drop the
user-defined type in ai-foundry-project.bicep. Both 0.15.0 and UDTs force
the compiled template into symbolic-name mode (languageVersion 2.0), where
the many same-named `existing` resourceGroups references collide during ARM
validation ("resourceGroup ... is defined multiple times"), breaking real
azd provision. 0.14.0 is the newest account version that supports
allowProjectManagement while compiling to classic mode.

Validated with a live `azd provision`: the AIServices account flips to a
Foundry account (allowProjectManagement=true) and the Foundry project is
created, with FOUNDRY_PROJECT_NAME / FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT populated.

author: (a person)
message:
fix(maf): two more columns whose absence rendered an empty track

The same shape as the `field5` guard, in the two places left:

- **`BigMafAdapter` read `feature.get('mafBlock') as string`.** The name comes
  from the file's own autoSql, so a BigBed that isn't a bigMaf hasn't got it —
  and the easiest way to hand it one is to put the `bigMafSummary.bb` its own
  `summaryAdapter` slot wants into `bigBedLocation`, since both are `.bb` files
  built from the same alignment.

- **`mafSummaryFeatures` read `f.get('src') as string`.** `src` is the whole
  mapping from a summary row to a display row: unmatched rows drop through
  `rowIndexBySrc` without a word, so a file lacking the column drew no bars at
  all. It matters more now than it did — the summary RPC discovers its row set
  from `src` when the track configures no samples, so an absent column would
  have produced a row literally named `undefined`.

Both now throw naming the column and the likely mix-up. Pinned against the
opposite file in each case: the summary `.bb` through `BigMafAdapter.getFeatures`,
and the alignment BED through the `summaryAdapter` slot.

`score` on a summary row was read with `!` and is now defaulted. Absent, the
alpha math turned `undefined` into `NaN` and an unpaintable fill; 0 shades the
bar at the `MIN_ALPHA` floor, which is what that floor exists for — a
low-scoring block still has to read as "this species aligns here".

author: (a person)
message:
Fix: Writing to a console emptied by deleteLine() no longer crashes (#10225)

#### Brief overview of PR changes/additions

`deleteLine()` on a console showing a single line leaves its buffer
holding zero lines. Three code paths then read the last line of that
buffer and abort:

- `TBuffer::append()` - `echo()`, `cecho()`, `decho()`, `hecho()`,
`echoLink()`, `appendBuffer()`, `insertText()`
- `TBuffer::commitLineData()` - game text arriving at the emptied
console
- `TConsole::printCommand()` - the echoed command, when a trigger
empties the buffer and sends

All three now seed a line with `appendEmptyLine()`, which is what the
sibling `appendLine()` and `appendFormatted()` already do.
`printCommand()` had a guard, but a dead one: `getLastLineNumber()`
returns 0 rather than -1 for an empty buffer, so its `>= 0` test never
fired.

New `EmptyBufferOps_spec.lua` drives all three paths, plus the rest of
the console API, against an emptied buffer.

#### Motivation for adding to Mudlet

Any script that clears a console down to nothing and then writes to it
takes the whole client down - a Qt assert in a debug build, an
out-of-bounds read in a release one. The likeliest way to hit it in the
wild is a gagging trigger on a multi-line packet, which the spec covers.

#### Other info (issues closed, discussion etc)

Closes #10207 (Echoing into a console emptied by `deleteLine()` crashes
Mudlet). That report covers `TBuffer::append()`; the other two came out
of checking the rest of the last-line reads, and were invisible in the
original report because the first crash aborts the run.

Full Lua suite passes (3792 successes, 0 failures). Each of the three
guards was individually reverted to confirm it is load-bearing - every
one aborts the suite on `ASSERT failure in QList::at: "index out of
range"`.

Not fixed here: `TTextEdit::keyPressEvent()` reads `lineBuffer.last()`
unguarded for Key_Down (`src/TTextEdit.cpp:4136`) and Ctrl+End
(`:4233`), which looks like the same class of bug on an emptied buffer.
Caret mode is F7-only with no Lua binding, so no spec can reach it and I
have not reproduced it - flagging rather than guarding speculatively.
